questions.scenario: A drafting agent writes a reply and a reviewing agent must check it afterwards. The order never changes.
questions.question: Which pattern should you use?

options.why: Correct. Agents run in a fixed order and pass output along.
Concurrent runs agents at the same time.
It is for open-ended work planned by a manager.
The order should be fixed.

questions.scenario: A billing agent and a delivery agent must analyse the same customer message at the same time, and the results are combined.
questions.question: Which pattern should you use?

options.why: The requirement is two specialists.
Correct. Both agents work in parallel and the results are aggregated.
It runs agents one after another.
It transfers control instead of merging parallel results.

questions.explanation: Concurrent fan-out saves time when tasks are independent.

questions.scenario: A triage agent must pass the conversation to whichever specialist agent suits the request.
questions.question: Which pattern should you use?

options.why: It runs all agents at once.
Batch is a deployment type, not an agent pattern.
Correct. Control moves to the better-suited agent.
It uses a fixed order.

questions.explanation: Handoff lets the conversation determine which agent responds.

questions.scenario: A research task has no known steps. A manager agent must create a plan, delegate tasks and track progress.
questions.question: Which pattern should you use?

options.why: It requires steps known in advance.
It does not plan.
It does not use specialists or a manager.
Correct. A manager plans and delegates open-ended work.

questions.scenario: A developer wants builders for sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat and Magentic orchestrations in Python.
questions.question: Which SDK provides them?

options.why: Correct. It includes orchestration builders.
This is a storage library.
This library is for Azure Language.
This is a management library for networks.

questions.explanation: Agent Framework offers orchestration patterns that you can combine with Foundry agents.
